instructions: Rinse the rice in a strainer until the water runs mostly clear. Add it to a small pot with 2 1/4 cups of cold tap water, bring to a boil, then cover and turn the heat to low. Cook for 15 minutes, then take it off the heat and leave the lid on.
Meanwhile, cut the mackerel into 2-inch pieces and pat them dry. Season them with the salt and 1/4 tsp of the pepper.
Thinly slice the onion and the shallots. Mince the garlic. Slice the green onions, keeping the white parts and the green parts in separate piles. Drain the pineapple.

Heat the oil and the sugar in a wide, deep skillet over medium heat, without stirring. After 2 to 3 minutes the sugar will melt and turn the color of dark amber. Don't walk away from it, because it goes from amber to bitter fast.
Add the onion, shallots and the white green-onion parts. Stir for 2 minutes, until they start to soften.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, until it smells good.
Add the pineapple and cook for 3 minutes, stirring now and then, until the edges start to brown.
Pour in the coconut water and the fish sauce. Bring it to a boil. Stand back a little, because the first whiff of fish sauce is strong.
Add the mackerel in a single layer. Spoon some of the sauce over the top. Turn the heat to medium-low, cover, and cook for 5 minutes.
Flip the pieces and cook, covered, for 5 minutes. The sauce should coat a spoon. If it's thin, take the lid off and let it bubble for a minute or two.
Take the pan off the heat. Sprinkle on the remaining 1/4 tsp pepper and the green parts of the green onions.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with the rice and a spoonful of the pineapple sauce over each bowl. Slice the Thai chilies and put them on the table for the adults.
method_notes: Both versions found by name (Helen's Recipes, Mama Snow Cooks) braise mackerel with pineapple, fish sauce and a sugar caramel, and finish with pepper and green onion over rice. Helen's is a plain caramel and fish sauce braise; Mama Snow Cooks builds the sauce on seared onion and shallot first, so this version takes that order. Neither page shows a rating and no trusted-cook version exists for it, so no rated lead was possible. Coconut water replaces the soda in one source and the chili moves to the table. Naturally gluten-free and dairy-free (fish sauce is gluten-free).
